name: Interference in Cobalt
description: A field of Riley-like cobalt and cream stripes that wakes straight and quiet, then through the day lets a slow set of concentric rings drift in across it, until by night the two systems lean, widen and cross into a full, breathing moire.
listening: The bass breath gently deepens the sway of the stripes, rising tension tightens the ring spacing towards the stripe spacing so the moire gathers before a chorus, treble sharpens the edges, the key leans the cream slightly towards the cobalt, each song sets a faintly different ring ellipse, and every hour's music energy is written into the thickness of the stripes at its own height, so by midnight the wall carries a stratified record of the day.

curator.verdict: A true op-art piece in cobalt and cream that breaks cleanly from the recent warm-glow-on-black run, with a legible arc from quiet stripes to full moire. It's bold for falling asleep to, and the 3 pm and 8 pm stills already read as dense checkerboards, so the arc peaks too early, but I would hang it.
